prompt: Use case: illustration-story / identity-preserving animation key poses. Make a production sprite atlas for an offline children's learning app. Polished friendly storybook animal illustration with soft shaded fur/feathers/scales, clear anatomy and expressive eyes, matching the reference style. ONE animal identity reused in ALL cells, camera/head size/body proportions/markings EXACTLY consistent. Every pose is full body, no cropped limbs. All face RIGHT unless subject says front-facing. Genuine transparent background, NO coloured paper/background, floor, panels, labels, letters, numbers, arrows, speech bubbles, motion lines, cast shadows or decorative objects. Equal square grid cells with 8% safe margins, consistent scale, same notional ground baseline 85% down each cell for grounded poses. The top LEFT cell is frame1 and order is row-major. Carefully articulate actual jaws/legs/wings/tails; do NOT simply rotate/scale the entire animal as a substitute.  Exactly 4 COLUMNS by 4 ROWS (16 poses). Empty spaces must have ALPHA ZERO, never a white/grey sheet or grid. Input reference is EXACT ANIMAL identity. The canonical golden-brown horse, black mane/tail, pale muzzle, white socks. Frames1–8 GALLOP: eight anatomically coherent phases of a side-on gallop, with alternating tucked legs, hind-leg push, extension, suspension and foreleg landing. Keep body/head fixed at same scale, four legs only, no rider/tack. Frames9–14 KICK: same horse facing RIGHT, brace front legs, lift the near hindleg, bend it, extend it backwards LEFT firmly, draw back, plant it. Frames15–16 rest standing closed/open eye. Do not stretch entire body to fake action.
